summary: Genus makes smart electricity meters that send readings to power distributors. On larger contracts it also fits the meters and keeps the reading system working.
description: Picture the meter outside a home. A smart meter measures electricity used and sends the reading to the distributor over a communications network. Genus builds the box and sells it to distributors and other installation firms. It also takes on longer jobs where it fits meters, connects them to the distributor’s billing system and keeps the equipment and software working.
money: On a supply order, Genus sells the meters. Under a longer project contract it is paid for work such as supplying and fitting meters and keeping the system working after launch. The bills it raises must cover parts, factory labour, installers, software, network fees and repairs before it earns a profit.
customers: The local electricity distributor buys meters or pays for a system that keeps delivering readings. Other companies that install and run meters also buy equipment from Genus. Households use the meters and pay their electricity bill or top-up to the distributor.
drivers: Look at how many meters customers accept, how much Genus spends to build and run them, and whether bills are paid on time.

quick.title: What does it do?
quick.text: It makes the meter that measures electricity use. It can also connect meters to a distributor’s billing system and keep them working.

quick.title: Who pays it?
quick.text: Electricity distributors and companies hired to fit and run meters. Households pay their electricity bills to the distributor.

quick.title: How does it earn?
quick.text: It sells meters. On longer contracts, it also gets paid to fit them and keep the system working.

quick.title: What does it spend money on?
quick.text: Electronic parts, factory and field workers, data connections, software and repairs.

groups.title: Electricity meters
groups.examples: Saksham-145 for smaller connections and Saksham-345 and Saksham-340 for larger loads.
groups.explanation: The device measures electricity as it enters a property and sends the readings to the electricity distributor. The distributor can use those readings to prepare bills.

groups.title: Prepaid meters
groups.examples: Agrim and other meters with prepaid options.
groups.explanation: A household can add credit before using electricity, much like topping up a mobile phone. The meter tracks electricity use against the available credit.

groups.title: Installation and operation
groups.examples: Replacing old meters and running the network and software that receive readings.
groups.explanation: A distributor can buy the full job. Teams fit and test meters, set up a link to the billing system, and fix equipment or connections when readings stop arriving.

groups.title: Software that checks meter readings
groups.examples: Software that receives and checks readings before sending them to the distributor’s billing system.
groups.explanation: A distributor can use the software to spot missing readings and find which meters need attention.

groups.title: Water and gas meters
groups.examples: Salil smart water meters and connected gas meters.
groups.explanation: A water meter measures how much water flows through a pipe. A gas meter measures how much gas is used. Both can send readings remotely.

basics.title: What makes a meter smart?
basics.text: It can report its readings remotely. The meter still measures the electricity used at that property. A network carries the reading to the distributor.

basics.title: What does a distributor do?
basics.text: It runs the local electricity lines and bills the homes and businesses connected to those lines. It can hire a company like Genus to measure usage and send the readings.

basics.title: What does an order book tell you?
basics.text: It shows work covered by orders and still to be done at a given date. Sales and cash arrive as work is completed, accepted and paid for.

stepsTitle: From fitting a meter to getting paid

steps.title: The distributor orders meters or a full system
steps.text: It sets the number of connections and the sort of readings it needs. A supply contract may end after the equipment is delivered and accepted.

steps.title: The project team fits and tests the meters
steps.text: On a full system job, installers replace the old boxes and check whether the new readings reach the distributor’s software.

steps.title: The system starts sending readings used for billing
steps.text: The customer checks and accepts the work. At each agreed stage, Genus sends its customer an invoice, which is a request for payment. On some projects that customer is the company hired by the distributor.

steps.title: Keep the system working and collect payments
steps.text: Teams repair faults and monitor readings while the project collects the payments due. Under contracts that require it, the project hands the system over to the distributor at the end.

specifics.title: The government programme matters
specifics.text: India’s Revamped Distribution Sector Scheme helps electricity distributors upgrade their networks, including fitting smart prepaid meters. Genus’s annual report says these projects are an important source of orders.

specifics.title: Genus can be both part-owner and contractor
specifics.text: Genus owns 26% of Gemstar Infra alongside an affiliate of GIC (an investment company owned by Singapore’s government). Gemstar controls separate companies that hold project contracts. They hire Genus to do work. Genus’s group profit also includes its share of earnings from part-owned companies.

specifics.title: An order is only the starting point
specifics.text: The latest filing includes work tied to Gemstar projects in the order book. Read that figure alongside meters fitted, systems accepted and customer payments.

watch: Are ordered meters reaching the point where customers accept them?
A meter ordered, one fitted and one sending usable readings are different stages.
Compare the company’s updates on the work remaining, meters fitted and systems brought into billing use.
How much cash is coming in after the work is billed?
Genus pays for equipment and workers before some customers pay.
Compare profit with cash from running the business. If bills customers still owe are growing, check whether cash is keeping up with sales.
The listed company partly owns a partner business and also works as a contractor for some projects.
Read the notes on Gemstar Infra to see which company holds each contract, which one borrows, and which one Genus bills for its work.
How are longer service contracts doing after launch?
A fitted meter earns its keep only while the customer can use its readings.
Check whether company updates distinguish running and maintaining systems from putting new meters in.
How dependent is Genus on a few customers?
Slow payment from a large customer can leave a lot of bills unpaid at once.
Read the annual report’s note on large customers alongside the amounts customers still owe.
risks: Elections, weather and limited access to premises can delay fitting and the start of service.
Readings fail to reach the distributor
Teams may need repeat visits if equipment or network links fail, and the distributor cannot bill using a reading it did not get.
Genus pays for parts and installers before it receives some payments. Late payment keeps its cash tied up for longer.
Changes to the public programme’s funding or deadlines could reduce or postpone orders.

helps.title: Factories serve several kinds of buyer
helps.text: Genus can supply its own projects and sell meters to distributors and other installation firms.

helps.title: Meters address several customer needs
helps.text: Distributors can buy meters for homes, larger buildings and parts of the local power network.

helps.title: Operating contracts can pay for years
helps.text: Where the contract covers upkeep, the distributor keeps paying for readings and a working system after the meters go in.

hurts.title: Low bids can leave little room for higher costs
hurts.text: Companies compete when distributors invite bids. A tight price leaves less room for higher costs for parts or labour.

hurts.title: Funding is needed before some work pays
hurts.text: Upfront equipment and field costs can require borrowing. Interest is due even if a project runs late.

hurts.title: A few customers account for much of sales
hurts.text: The annual report shows that several large customers together account for more than half of annual revenue. Losing a large contract would affect the amount of work available.

financialNotes.title: Read the group totals
financialNotes.text: The audited year ended 31 March 2026 is reported for the group in rupees crore. The reported net profit includes the share of profit of some part-owned companies, while those companies’ full sales are outside group revenue.

financialNotes.title: Compare sales with cash collected
financialNotes.text: Genus reports metering and related services as one business. The annual filing breaks out types of sales, including goods, services and some long contracts. Read that note alongside the cash from running the business and the amounts customers still owe.

financialCue: Compare revenue with group profit, then see which sales the filing describes as goods, services or long project contracts.
